punchline: James Allen noticed that in a garden you have to put the good seeds in, but the weed-seeds simply fall in by themselves.
thirty_sec: In 1903 James Allen wrote a little book comparing the mind to a garden. Tend it or ignore it, something will grow. If you don't put useful seeds in, weed-seeds fall in on their own and keep multiplying. He even picks the verbs carefully: good seeds are put, weeds fall. A person who keeps weeding becomes, in his words, the master-gardener of their soul. Corn gives corn, nettles give nettles.
